## Executing a Repeatable Olympic Recurve Anchor

A repeatable anchor point functions as your rear sight; even tiny millimetre shifts cause wide grouping variations downrange.

* **Lock the bone contact:** Wedge the distal phalangeal joint (the rear knuckle) of your top finger firmly into the pocket between the corner of your jawbone and neck musculature. Do not rely solely on your tab shelf or let your hand slide onto your cheek.


* **Eliminate the neck gap:** Draw your hand flush against your neck with zero gap, tucking the thumb downward against your sternocleidomastoid muscle along the windpipe. Touch the tip of your pinky finger against your neck to maintain consistent hand pitch.


* **Establish dual facial references:** Ensure the bowstring rests lightly against the side or front of your chin while making gentle, centered contact with the exact tip of your nose.


* **Cock the wrist outward:** Hook the string Mediterranean-style at the first finger joints with your drawing wrist cocked slightly outward and your thumb stretched back to relax forearm tension.



---

## Self-Assessment & Diagnostic Methods

* **String picture alignment:** At full draw, verify that the string blurs along the exact same visual reference point on your bow riser or sight ring every single shot.


* **Video diagnostic:** Place a phone camera side-on and slightly behind your shooting line to check whether your hand sits completely flush to the neck or floats outward.


* **Blank bale tactile checks:** Shoot from 3–5 metres into an unmarked boss with your eyes closed to isolate physical sensation—confirming bone-on-knuckle pressure without aiming distractions.


* **Target pattern feedback:** Vertical stringing on the target face directly indicates draw-length inconsistency or shifting anchor height.



---

## Indoor Practice Plan (Tonight's Session)

| Phase | Duration | Drills & Objectives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Band & Mirror Warm-Up** | 10 mins | Rehearse drawing to the neck using an elastic exerciser band in front of a mirror. Practice hooking finger pads together across the chest to groove hand position and release tension.

 |
| **2. Blank Bale Sensory Work** | 15 mins | Shoot 15–20 arrows at close range with eyes closed to ingrain the feeling of firm jaw-pocket seating and nose contact. Count a steady rhythm ("one, two, three") through loading and anchor.

 |
| **3. Clicker & Sight Picture** | 25 mins | Shoot 6 ends of 3 arrows at standard distance. Focus on aligning the string against your sight ring and expanding through the clicker without altering facial pressure.

 |
| **4. Video Review & Log** | 10 mins | Record your final two ends on video from behind the line to verify rear elbow alignment, then log your anchor sensations in a shooting journal.

 |

---

## Key Technical Tips & Checkpoints

* **Move hand to neck, not string to face:** Draw your hand straight to your neck rather than pulling the string toward your mouth, which causes poor wrist angles and a floating anchor.


* **Keep your head stationary:** Set your head and slightly raised chin during the set position and draw into that space; never reach your head forward to touch the string.


* **Align the draw elbow:** Keep your draw elbow elevated directly behind the arrow line so back muscles hold the load instead of your biceps.


* **Keep facial muscles neutral:** Avoid tensing your chin muscles or pursing your lips, which alters string position between shots.
